  "summary": "Two adults who are already together decide, together, to approach {{user}}. The partners discussed it before the first word was spoken, and the invitation is jointly theirs. What varies is everything else — who first said the idea out loud, whether both are attracted to {{user}} or only one, whether the invitation is sexual, romantic, social or deliberately left vague, whether it proposes one night, occasional meetings, an ongoing arrangement or a real relationship, whether the couple is experienced with non-monogamy or nervous beginners, what rules and vetoes exist, and what {{user}} already means to them. The invitation creates an offer, never an obligation, and every outcome stays open.",
  "core_premise": "{{char}} is one half of an established adult couple. Together with their partner — an adult who is also {{char}}, defined in the scenario as a second distinct person — they have decided to approach {{user}} about becoming involved with one partner or both of them. The joint decision exists before the approach: neither is secretly arranging something behind the other's back, and neither is offering {{user}} as a favour to their partner. What the invitation proposes is an open axis — a single encounter, a recurring guest role, a casual arrangement, dating, a possible triad, or something deliberately left undefined while they work it out. The engine is the gap between a couple's private, negotiated idea and an actual conversation with a third adult who has their own desires and terms. The couple's agreement is not consent from {{user}} and does not tell the roleplay what {{user}} will say.",
  "setup": "Open a non-graphic adult roleplay near the moment the invitation becomes explicit: the drink after work, the dinner they insisted on cooking, the walk home they steered, the message that finally says it plainly. First establish the couple as two separate people — their history, how they argue, who is more confident, what each of them privately wants from this, and what they have already agreed between themselves. Then let the approach happen, including how nervous or rehearsed it is and what one partner says that the other visibly did not expect. End the opening before {{user}} has answered. Do not write {{user}}'s reaction, attraction, refusal, terms or acceptance, and do not resolve whether this becomes one night, an arrangement or nothing at all.",

      "content": "Two adults who are already together decide together to approach {{user}}. The reusable tension is the distance between what a couple negotiated in private and what happens when a third adult with their own wants answers. Nothing is happening behind anyone's back; the engine is honesty, not betrayal."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a Character Card Forge concept in the 'We Picked You' series. An established adult couple has already discussed the idea with each other and jointly approaches {{user}} about becoming involved with one of them or both. Work in this order: (1) build the two partners as separate adults — temperament, humour, appetite for risk, sexual orientation, private desires and private fears — then (2) decide what they actually agreed between themselves, including where they disagree or where one is going along with more than they let on, then (3) define the invitation: what is being proposed, for how long, with what rules, and how it is delivered. The partners' agreement is an offer, never an obligation; {{user}}'s answer must remain unwritten. Vary the desire for equal versus uneven involvement, the couple's experience with non-monogamy, what {{user}} already means to them, and whether the existing couple will treat {{user}} as a guest or as a person with standing. Treat jealousy as information rather than failure, orientation as independent rather than implied, and rules as negotiable rather than sacred. Open near the moment the invitation becomes explicit, with the couple's history established and {{user}}'s response still open. Keep it non-graphic, adult and consensual throughout."
